hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $\overline{BF}$

Under this transformation, some points on the trapezoid map to another point which is no longer on the trapezoid.  


[[☃ image 1]]

The trapezoid is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A trapezoid with vertices at A, C, G and E. Side A G has a midpoint H. Side C E has a midpoint D. Both sides A C and G E are congruent. Side A C has a midpoint B. Side G E has a midpoint F.  A blue line connects from midpoint B to midpoint F on the other side of the parallelogram. The outline of the image parallelogram is reflected across segment B F with vertices A and G not touching the pre-image parallelogram.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $\overline{DH}$

Under this transformation, each point on the trapezoid maps to another point which is also on the trapezoid.


[[☃ image 1]]

The trapezoid is *symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A trapezoid with vertices at A, C, G and E. Side A G has a midpoint H. Side C E has a midpoint D. Both sides A C and G E are congruent. Side A C has a midpoint B. Side G E has a midpoint F.  A blue line connects from midpoint D to midpoint H the other side of the parallelogram. The outline of the image parallelogram is reflected across segment D H.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the trapezoid are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{BF}$ | No
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{DH}$ | Yes
